From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: FinBank security & KMS follow-up

Hi Tom -

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we're aligned: 

What we heard (FinBank priorities):
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and regular attestation cadence
- HIPAA applicability for certain data workflows and need for BAAs
- Customer-controlled encryption (CMEK) / HSM-backed keys for high-sensitivity workloads
- Proof points for in-transit and at-rest encryption and key handling

What we'll provide by EOD tomorrow:
- SOC 2 summary + link to the full report (redacted where appropriate) - attached
- Vendor security questionnaire (we'll return the first pass), + a copy for your procurement team - attached
- Short KMS FAQ explaining hosted KMS vs customer-managed keys and which deployments support HSM

Technical note (high level):
- At-rest: AES-256 by default for models/data stored on Redwood-managed storage.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ between clients and the control plane; mTLS available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- KMS/CMK options: Hosted KMS (Redwood-managed) for hosted API; Customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (BYOK) or CloudHSM for Dedicated/Private. See attached FAQ for details.

Next steps / asks from you:
1) Can you confirm whether FinBank needs HSM-backed keys for the initial pilot or if AWS KMS with a CMK is sufficient?
2) Please upload the vendor security questionnaire we send into your procurement portal and let us know any high-priority redlines.
3) If helpful, we can arrange a short technical call with Camila (SE) this week to walk through the KMS options.

Cc'ing Camila and Marissa to handle the technical questionnaire and procurement coordination.

Thanks -
Rachel

- FinBank will almost certainly require HSM-backed keys for production access to sensitive PII workflows. For the pilot, we may accept AWS KMS CMK if we can confirm CloudHSM-backed key origins.
- We need SOC 2 Type II (most recent) and confirmation that Redwood is willing to execute a BAA if we surface PHI during the integration.
- Timeline for questionnaire? Procurement needs an initial response within 3 business days.

Subject: Re: Post-call: FinBank security & KMS follow-up

Tom - thanks for the follow-up. Quick answers (technical):

> For the pilot, we may accept AWS KMS CMK if we can confirm CloudHSM-backed key origins.
- Correct. For Hosted API customers we offer Redwood-managed keys (AES-256 at rest) and a BYOK flow that integrates with AWS KMS. If your KMS keys are backed by AWS CloudHSM (i.e., generated in a CloudHSM cluster and imported to KMS or configured with KMS key origin = AWS_CLOUDHSM), that satisfies the HSM-backed requirement.

> Will Redwood execute a BAA if we surface PHI?
- Yes - we do sign BAAs for customers with covered PHI. We'll route that to our Legal team; Marissa has handled BAAs previously and will own that thread.

Technical specifics (short):
- At-rest encryption: AES-256 with per-blob envelope encryption keys. Keys for Redwood-managed KMS are stored in our provider-managed KMS.
- CMEK/BYOK: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we support BYOK via AWS KMS integration (customer-controlled CMKs).
- HSM support: HSM-backed keys are available when keys originate in CloudHSM or when customers manage keys in a CloudHSM-backed KMS (Dedicated/Private gives tighter controls and no key export).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+; inter-node traffic in Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured for mTLS and private networking (VPC).

Attached: short KMS FAQ + the vendor security questionnaire (initial draft filled). I've redacted internal details.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rachel - can you share SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and the DPA template?
2) Tom - if procurement needs a completed questionnaire within 3 business days, I'll prioritize the outstanding items and suggest a 30-min technical handoff on Tue 3/17 or Wed 3/18. Which works?

Thanks,
Camila
